description: This grouped bar chart illustrates the "Number of datasets" published across different years, categorized by "Researcher Location." The horizontal category axis is labeled "Year" and displays a chronological sequence from 2012 to 2022. The vertical value axis is labeled "Number of datasets" and utilizes a logarithmic scale ranging from $10^0$ to above $10^2$, with major grid lines and tick marks at intervals of powers of ten ($10^0$, $10^1$, $10^2$). The data is represented by sets of bars grouped side-by-side for each year. According to the legend, the colors correspond to specific researcher locations: "Other" (blue), "USA" (orange), "IN" (green), "UK" (red), "IT" (purple), and "DE" (brown). The number of bars within each yearly group varies depending on the available data for that year, starting with single or dual bars in early years like 2012 and 2013 (where the USA bar is slightly above $10^0$), and expanding to include all six categories in years like 2017 through 2021. The shortest bars in the chart align closely with the $10^0$ mark, representing a value of approximately 1, seen in instances such as USA in 2014, DE in 2015, and IT in 2022. The tallest bar represents the "Other" category in the year 2020, extending significantly above the $10^2$ line. The categories on the x-axis are sorted chronologically. Notably, the entire chart is rendered at a tilted angle, and the bars corresponding to the final year, 2022, are visually distinguished by being rendered with lower opacity compared to the solid colors of the preceding years.
